name: EK3_ALT_M_NSE
notes: Baro height measurement noise. Writable (clamped 2-10) rather than read-only because the EKF falls back to baro automatically whenever GPS height is lost - AP_NavEKF3_PosVelFusion.cpp lostGpsHgt - so this governs height fusion on every unit during a GPS dropout, not only when EK3_SRCx_POSZ selects baro. Raising it de-weights a noisy baro (rotor wash, enclosure pressure), which is the direction field fixes have needed. The clamp floor is the seeded default: lowering it below 2 makes the filter over-trust baro and is the divergence case. Only affects fusion when the active height source is baro; with EK3_SRC1_POSZ=3 (GPS) the GPS branch uses receiver vertical accuracy instead.

name: FFT_ENABLE
notes: Writable so FFT data can be collected during custom integration work. Safe on the control path: INS_HNTCH_MODE is 1 (throttle-based) and read-only, so the FFT analyser only logs and never drives the harmonic notch (that would need mode 4). MANIFEST DEBT: this param carries AP_PARAM_FLAG_ENABLE, so setting it to 1 and rebooting exposes 14 more FFT_ params (MINHZ MAXHZ SAMPLE_MODE WINDOW_SIZE WINDOW_OLAP FREQ_HOVER THR_REF SNR_REF ATT_REF BW_HOVER HMNC_FIT HMNC_PEAK NUM_FRAMES OPTIONS), all writable and unclamped because none are seeded in defaults.parm. They are absent from param_manifest.txt and --check cannot catch it (it only flags defaults.parm entries missing from the manifest, not feature-gated params). Take a param download with FFT_ENABLE=1 and add them. Watch FFT_MAXHZ: exceeding Nyquist blocks arming via AP_GyroFFT pre_arm_check.

name: FS_DR_ENABLE
notes: Land (1), changed from RTL (2). Deadreckoning propagates position on the EKF wind estimate, but drag fusion is off (EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_X/Y and EK3_DRAG_MCOEF all 0), so there is no wind observation to dead reckon against - the estimate is essentially unconstrained, not merely degraded. RTL would climb to RTL_ALT 50m and transit up to ~240m at WPNAV_SPEED 8m/s on that estimate. Note the action is bounded either way: FS_DR_TIMEOUT 30 gates ekf_has_relative_position (ArduCopter/system.cpp), so after 30s the EKF failsafe fires and FS_EKF_ACTION 1 lands it regardless - the choice is only whether to spend those 30s transiting blind. Landing keeps the aircraft near the operator's visual reference and preserves manual recovery via AltHold. Exposure is high because there is no position redundancy: single Here4 (GPS1_TYPE 9, GPS2_TYPE 0) and EK3_SRC2/3_POSXY are both 0. Fires in Guided, which is where the figure-8 applet flies. Revisit if Xplorer starts operating beyond visual line of sight, where a wrong-but-homeward heading may beat a correct-but-local one.

name: PSC_ACCZ_D
notes: Position/velocity/accel controller gain - deliberately @READONLY in shipping builds. Param review asked whether to open the PSC_ block for loiter tuning; decision is that production stays locked and only dev builds open them. name: RC1_REVERSED
notes: Roll/pitch/throttle/yaw channel reversal - @READONLY because a flipped primary control channel is immediately unflyable and there is no pre-arm check that would catch it (0 and 1 are both valid values). RC1-4 MIN/MAX/TRIM/DZ are deliberately left writable so the normal GCS radio calibration sweep still works; reversal is a separate manual toggle in MP/QGC, not part of that sweep, so locking it does not break calibration. If a customer transmitter genuinely has an inverted channel the fix belongs on the transmitter, not in the flight controller. RC5-8_REVERSED are locked on the same reasoning; RC9-RC16_REVERSED remain writable (payload/gimbal channels).

name: RC5_REVERSED
notes: Mode-switch channel reversal - @READONLY. These four channels carry the flight mode switches (RC5_OPTION 70 alt hold, RC6_OPTION 56 loiter, RC7_OPTION 4 RTL, RC8_OPTION 16 Auto), and those _OPTION assignments are already locked. Leaving REVERSED writable left a gap: flipping it inverts which switch position selects the mode, so the pilot reaching for RTL would get the opposite. Same class of problem as RC1-4 and closed for the same reason. RC9-RC16_REVERSED remain writable - those are payload/gimbal channels (wheel yaw, wheel pitch, camera trigger, mount lock), where a reversal is an annoyance rather than a flight-safety issue.
